title: When the Cover Burns
premise: When Noor Galloway's former handler, Elias Voss, is found dead hours after sending him a meeting invitation dated for the next day, Noor attends anyway and finds a dead-drop containing evidence that the 'incident' that broke his career was staged to bury a covert arms pipeline run through three governments' intelligence services. Hunted by an assassin codenamed Meridian and betrayed by the agency he served, Noor assembles an unlikely crew — a disgraced forensic accountant, a defected courier, and the daughter Voss never acknowledged — into a found family bound by grief and purpose. Unable to trust courts or agencies, they leak the truth through a hostage negotiation of their own design: taking a black-site broker alive and trading his testimony for global broadcast. The book ends with the pipeline exposed, Meridian choosing justice over contract at the last moment, and Noor finally sleeping through the night.
about_author: O. M. Nystrom is the pen name of a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to people talk their way out of the worst nights of their lives. They write thrillers about the quiet mechanics of persuasion and the families people build when institutions fail them.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Noor Galloway, insomniac and sidelined after the Marrow Street incident, receives a calendar invite for tomorrow morning from Elias Voss — then learns Voss died this afternoon. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into compulsion; he decides to attend.

chapters.title: Empty Chair
chapters.summary: At a riverside café, Noor finds no Voss but a locker key taped under the table. Watching him from across the street is a woman who leaves when he does. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: paranoia blooming; the sense that the meeting is happening whether or not anyone shows.

chapters.title: What Voss Left Behind
chapters.summary: The locker holds a drive and a handwritten note: 'Marrow Street wasn't your failure.' The files sketch a weapons pipeline laundered through three governments — and name the operation that staged the incident. POV: Noor with a brief interlude from the watcher, Ilsa Voss, his daughter. Emotional beat: vindication curdling into terror.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Introduce the assassin: precise, patient, contracted to recover the drive and erase everyone who touched it. She studies Noor's file and hesitates over one detail — his negotiation transcripts. POV: Meridian. Emotional beat: cold professionalism disturbed by an unfamiliar curiosity.

chapters.title: The Accountant Who Counts Sins
chapters.summary: Noor tracks down Priya Raghavan, a forensic accountant whose conviction was engineered by the same network. She confirms the money trail in ninety seconds flat. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: bitter humor masking a hunger for reckoning; she joins him.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Holed up in a decommissioned ferry terminal, Noor, Priya, and Ilsa — who reveals herself and her father's double life — set rules and divide the files. First assassination attempt on Noor fails by minutes. POV: rotating. Emotional beat: three strangers becoming a unit under fire.

chapters.title: The Courier's Defection
chapters.summary: Tomas Reyes, a courier who moved the pipeline's physical ledgers, defects to them carrying proof of a black-site broker called the Quartermaster. Meridian kills his escort but lets Tomas live — off-script. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: guilt-driven courage; the family grows by one.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Priya maps how each government used the pipeline while denouncing it; Noor realizes no court can touch it without someone being sacrificed first. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: despair at institutional rot, hardening into resolve to go outside the law.

chapters.title: The Trap at Marrow Street
chapters.summary: Noor returns to the site of his failure and reconstructs the incident: the hostage-taker was a patsy, the call scripted. He breaks — then rebuilds himself around the truth. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: the book's emotional nadir and turning point; grief becomes fuel.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Meridian corners Noor alone. Instead of fighting, he negotiates — reading her file's hesitation aloud, offering her a choice no contractor has ever given her. She walks away without the drive. POV: alternating Noor/Meridian. Emotional beat: the thriller's signature scene; two professionals recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: The agency brands Noor a rogue asset; his face hits every watchlist. Ilsa uses her father's old contacts to move the team across borders like ghosts. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: the found family fully forms — loyalty chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: The Quartermaster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas decodes the physical ledgers: names, dates, one live black-site facility where the Quartermaster operates. The team debates the impossible plan forming in Noor's head. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: fear and audacity in equal measure; the plan takes shape.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Hostage Crisis
chapters.summary: Noor trains the team for their inversion: they will take the Quartermaster himself, hold him, and negotiate his testimony to the world. Priya objects to the ethics; Noor answers with Marrow Street. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: moral weight accepted knowingly; justice outside the law defined.

chapters.title: Infiltration
chapters.summary: Using a scheduled supply rotation, the team breaches the facility. Everything goes right until a second security layer appears that isn't in any ledger. POV: rotating. Emotional beat: white-knuckle tension; competence against chaos.

chapters.title: The Man in the Middle Room
chapters.summary: They find the Quartermaster — and discover he expected them; Voss had contacted him before dying. The old broker offers a deal: his testimony for his life. POV: the Quartermaster. Emotional beat: unsettling charm; the enemy more human than expected.

chapters.title: Siege
chapters.summary: Agency strike teams surround the facility. Noor, the negotiator, now negotiates for his own family's lives — talking down a commander who once was his friend. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: full-circle mastery; his greatest skill turned to survival.

chapters.title: Meridian Returns
chapters.summary: Meridian infiltrates the siege — contracted again, this time for all of them. She reaches the command room where Noor stands between her rifle and the Quartermaster. POV: Meridian. Emotional beat: the assassin's choice crystallizing; she lowers the weapon and gives them the strike teams' approach plan instead.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Priya streams the Quartermaster's testimony and the ledgers simultaneously across three continents before the signal can be killed. Governments scramble; denials collapse in real time. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: catharsis — truth escaping the cage at last.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: With the world watching, killing them becomes worse than freeing them. The strike commander stands down; the team walks out under a hundred cameras. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: disbelief giving way to triumph; the family survives its own plan.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Inquiries open; careers burn; Noor's record is quietly corrected. The Quartermaster enters protective custody, testifying in exchange for years, not death. Meridian vanishes, leaving only a note: 'Debt paid.' POV: rotating. Emotional beat: bittersweet accounting — justice done, wounds remaining.

chapters.title: Voss's Grave
chapters.summary: The four of them bury Elias Voss properly, with his real name spoken aloud. Ilsa reads the letter he never sent. Each of them stays afterward longer than they need to. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: mourning completed; inheritance understood as memory, not money.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Months later, Noor trains new negotiators, teaching the lesson Marrow Street taught him: listen for what isn't said. That night, unremarkably, he sleeps until morning. Final image: the calendar app, empty except for dinner with three friends. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; the incident finally off the board.
